do_more: Focus topics directly on observable human behavior and body language (e.g., facial expressions, reading emotions, posture).
Use direct, clear book/concept titles with structural subtitles (e.g., 'Book Title · Sub-topic · Reading X') rather than clickbait essay-style titles.
Keep Short scripts tight (closer to 30 seconds) to maximize completion rate and initial swipe-away retention.
Hook viewers using universal human experiences (emotions, habits, memory, focus) rather than historical or academic context.
avoid: Avoid meta- commentary titles, clickbait phrasing, or emoji-heavy headlines (e.g., 'The psychology of...', 'here's how 🎯').
Avoid framing psychology through historical figures, Victorian literature, or academic origins (e.g., Galton, Le Bon, 1890 blueprints).
Avoid vague or overly broad topics like public speaking or corporate/industrial efficiency.
short.title_style: Simple, authoritative book titles paired with specific, intriguing sub-topics (e.g., 'The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals · Watching expression · Reading 5') perform drastically better than generic modern clickbait titles.
next_tests: Test a 30-second vs. 45-second script using the exact same excerpt from Darwin's 'Expression of the Emotions' to confirm optimal retention length.
Test framing classic passages as immediate self-discovery tools (e.g., 'Why you express X') versus standard reading formats to see if direct personal relevance boosts shares.
short.best_title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals · Watching expression · Reading 5

Use structured naming conventions like 'Reading X' combined with a clear thematic subtitle to set viewer expectations.
Target applied and behavioral psychology domains such as industrial efficiency and visible human emotions.
Keep initial titles punchy and focused on direct cognitive phenomena.
avoid: Avoid dense, abstract overarching topics like 'A General Introduction to Psychoanalysis' or 'The Psychology of Revolution' for full-length formats.

Avoid long, dry academic titles without a clear behavioral hook.
full.title_style: Winning titles pair a recognized classic author or domain with a concrete, observable human behavior or specific reading part rather than a generic book title.
next_tests: Test a full-length video focused entirely on practical workplace behavior using the industrial efficiency framework.
Test titling a psychoanalysis concept around a specific daily habit instead of an academic introduction.
Compare performance between multi-part reading sequences versus standalone behavioral deep dives.
